name: Lundgren set covering
note: https://github.com/hakank/hakank/blob/master/cpmpy/set_covering4.py (Lundgren, Ronnqvist, Varbrand, 'Optimeringslara', p. 408), set covering variant: 10 alternatives as media with their costs, 8 objects as audiences, so incidence_matrix is the transpose of the source's alternative-by-object table. The source states a unique optimum of 45 (alternatives 4, 8 and 10).

name: Taha security telephones
note: https://github.com/hakank/hakank/blob/master/cpmpy/set_covering2.py (Taha, 'Operations Research - An Introduction', Example 9.1-2): 8 street corners as media, 11 streets as audiences, each street covered by the telephones at its two corners (1-based corners in the source, 0-based here). The source minimises the number of telephones, so every media cost is 1.

name: Winston fire stations
note: https://github.com/hakank/hakank/blob/master/cpmpy/set_covering.py (Winston, 'Operations Research', p. 486): 6 cities, a station in city j covers city i when their distance is at most 15; cities as both audiences and media, every media cost 1 because the source minimises the number of stations.

name: generated 12 audiences 9 media
note: generated: after Python random.seed(5), incidence rows drawn with random.random() < 0.3 per entry (12 audiences x 9 media), redrawn as a whole until every audience has a medium; then costs random.randint(5, 40). Unequal costs, so the fewest media is not the cheapest cover.
